sources.title: A study of sequence weighting at scale

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: Random log-uniform sequence weights range from 0.01 to 10; evaluation follows three training epochs. Validation tuning and regularization accompany improving held-out performance across scale.
The exponent often rises then falls across model size; shared and specific patterns are a hypothesis. Inverse-exponent weight compensation remains untested.

sources.project_implication: Useful held-out adaptation and a component mechanism are needed for a stronger alignment claim.
limitations: Private benchmark and in-house models prevent an exact local reproduction.
Reported scaling patterns are empirical; the mechanism is proposed.

sources.title: An estimator for the effective sequence weight exponent
sources.author_attribution_note: The one-page PDF has no author byline; published alongside the Renda-Mani Jane Street blog.
sources.publication_status: Undated technical note attached to Jane Street blog
inspected: Complete one-page note: population definition, finite estimator, final remark

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: Optimization is over p>=0 with E[G]>0; individual gains may be negative.

Normalized gains and weight powers enter a percentile-rank kernel. The note states asymptotic recovery for an exact conditional power law and distinguishes its misspecified target from nonlinear least squares.

sources.project_implication: Our finite interval, numerical guard and finite-sample stress tests require separate interpretation.
limitations: No implementation source was inspected; local numerical findings do not establish an upstream bug.
The note does not supply our 1e-10 guard or p<=8 restriction.

sources.title: What is the Effect of Importance Weighting in Deep Learning?
sources.date_precision: Conference held 9-15 June 2019; no exact article publication day asserted

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: Weighting effects diminish over epochs in the studied deep-learning settings; L2 regularization and batch normalization restore some effect, unlike dropout in those experiments.

sources.project_implication: Duration and regularization dependence is prior work; the project can contribute a narrower controlled validation-selection case study.
limitations: This abstract-level review does not establish identical training regimes or metrics.
Its general phenomenon should not be redescribed as our new discovery.

sources.title: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Separable Data
inspected: JMLR metadata and abstract; publication month in paper header

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: For unregularized logistic regression with homogeneous linear predictors and linearly separable data, gradient descent approaches the maximum-margin direction; the paper gives specified extensions and slow convergence.

sources.project_implication: Use as theoretical background while separating its assumptions from finite Transformer training.
limitations: Does not directly prove a sequence-loss-gain exponent law for AdamW Transformers.

sources.title: Understanding the role of importance weighting for deep learning
sources.publication_status: ICLR 2021, as stated on paper first page

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: For the specified separable linear setting, weights can change finite-step convergence while preserving the asymptotic direction.
The analysis states homogeneity, loss-tail and regularity assumptions and relates importance weighting to margins and distribution shift.

sources.project_implication: Optimizer, stopping time and capacity should be separated before assigning a mechanism.
limitations: The theorem assumptions were inspected but not proved applicable to the local Transformer/AdamW setup.

sources.title: Is Importance Weighting Incompatible with Interpolating Classifiers?
inspected: Primary OpenReview PDF indexed first-page excerpt

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: Polynomially tailed losses restore importance-weight effects in their analysis and experiments; exponentiating classical importance weights can help in the specified shift setting.

sources.project_implication: Loss choice and prior exponentiation methods constrain broad novelty claims about compensation.
limitations: OpenReview direct access returned browser verification; accessible arXiv supplied the primary record.
Distribution-shift importance weights are distinct from this project's randomized sequence weights.

sources.title: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models
sources.publication_status: NeurIPS 2023; inspected current arXiv v5 record
inspected: arXiv abstract, authors, version dates; proceedings record

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: Experiments model diminishing returns from repeated tokens and excess parameters under limited unique data, with a compute-optimal scaling law.

sources.project_implication: Repetition and compute budgets must be explicit when comparing weighting and scaling results.
limitations: Whole-dataset repetition and compute-optimal loss are different interventions and outcomes from p* on a fixed adaptation dataset.

sources.title: Scaling Domain Data Repetition in LLM Pretraining
inspected: Abstract and metadata; linked directly by Jane Street

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: At fixed tokens per parameter, optimal domain repetition mildly increases with model size; repetition optima vary with domain validation loss.

sources.project_implication: Prespecify budget normalization and separate domain repetition optima from the effective sequence exponent.
limitations: Preprint status retained; the result does not predict our finite synthetic capacity contrast.

sources.title: Internal Data Repetition Destroys Language Models
sources.publication_status: arXiv preprint; no main-conference status asserted

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: At fixed compute allocated to duplicates, evaluation loss peaks at an intermediate repeat count; a misspecified linear model reproduces a qualitative loss peak.

sources.project_implication: A nonmonotonicity or memorization-generalization trade-off claim alone has substantial prior overlap.
limitations: The outcome is evaluation loss as repetition changes, rather than the sequence-weight exponent as capacity changes.
Abstract-level review; no theorem or numerical result is imported into our setting.

sources.title: Data Repetition Beats Data Scaling in Long-CoT Supervised Fine-Tuning

supported_claims.support_paraphrase: At fixed update budget, repeated reasoning examples outperform larger single-pass datasets in the reported settings, and improvements plateau near complete training memorization.

sources.project_implication: Keep synthetic utility failures local; memorization need not universally imply worse generalization.
limitations: Reasoning supervised fine-tuning is distinct from our answer-token synthetic task.
Abstract-level review; no claim that its stopping rule transfers to our experiment.

review_limits: Focused selection of ten primary sources, not an exhaustive related-work survey.
No secondary summaries serve as evidence for retained claims.
Ancillary literature claims are primarily abstract-level; direct theorem applicability was not established.
No new estimator, exact large-LM replication, Jane Street implementation bug, universal scaling law, useful compensation algorithm or publication guarantee is established.
Source versions and findings may change after the access date; refresh before submission.
